ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all direct and indirect shareholders, directors, managers and UBOs against Luxembourg domestic sanctions lists, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions, and OFAC SDN List; PEP designation is required under the Law of 12 November 2004 (Article 3(13)); enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and transactions transmitted via non-bank payment rails. AML risk tier for this ISIC 6201 activity is standard low-risk, but full CDD remains statutory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin script; the name may be in French, German, Luxembourgish or another language provided it uses Latin characters; it must not be misleading, contrary to public order or identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name; a limited liability company must contain 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'S.à r.l.' or 'SARL' in its name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative request for reconsideration with the Luxembourg Business Registers and, within one month, an appeal to the administrative tribunal (Tribunal administratif) for review of the refusal. No extension of the reservation period is granted after filing of the official corporate law documents; a fresh name reservation must be made for any subsequent application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a licensed corporate-domiciliation agent that maintains a physical address; a pure virtual office or PO Box is not permissible. The actual software-development and integrity-middleware business requires physical or verifiable operational substance; therefore a service-agreement with a domiciliation agent is acceptable only for the initial incorporation and registration phase.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate (estimated 15-25%) in the first three years of operation, driven by corporate-tax substance requirements, UBO-register verifications and occasional AML spot checks by the CSSF or the Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF); unannounced inspections occur in response to discrepancies in RBE filings or sanctioned persons alerts.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended, Title V on the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (Arts. 180 to 192-17); modernised by the Law of 10 August 2016; complementing provisions of the Law of 13 December 2023 on the business register and corporate transparency; Civil Code Arts. 1832 et seq. for general company contracts.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), 9-13 Rue du Château d'Eau, L-3364 Leudelange, Luxembourg; filings made electronically via the LBR extranet portal (www.lbr.lu).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif notarié — notarially executed Deed of Incorporation, accompanied by the statutory annexes (pièces) and the RCS registration application e-filed by the Luxembourg notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital for an S.A.R.L. is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed at incorporation. Each cash quota must be paid up to at least 50% at formation, with the balance payable within five years; in-kind contributions must be fully paid up and described in the notarial deed. For this Stage 2 workflow the entire EUR 12,000 is deposited on a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) in the name of 'LU SARL — société en formation'; the bank's blocked-funds certificate (attestation de blocage) is delivered to the notary before execution, and the funds are released to the Company upon presentation of the RCS registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned Founders, acting as sole shareholders of the Company in formation ('LU SARL'), hereby approve the draft Articles of Association; subscribe for all two hundred and forty quotas representing EUR 12,000 of fully subscribed share capital, the legal minimum paid-up portion being blocked in escrow with the depositary bank; adopt the registered office at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; appoint [Name] as sole Manager (Gérant), hereby accepting office, with full powers to manage, represent, bind the Company, and open bank accounts; authorize the Manager to execute the notarial deed, complete RCS registration and RESA publication, and carry out tax, VAT and social security formalities; and ratify all preliminary acts performed on behalf of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Blocked Capital Account and KYC Clearance at a CSSF-Regulated Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), acting as depositary of the share capital (e.g. major Luxembourg clearing banks or private banks with corporate desks).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the draft Articles of Association and the founders' KYC pack. Open a blocked escrow account in the name of 'LU SARL — société en formation' and deposit EUR 12,000. Instruct the bank to issue an attestation de blocage de fonds (blocked-funds certificate) addressed to the Luxembourg notary, dated no earlier than two business days before the deed execution date. The bank will place a blocking instruction releasing the funds only upon production of the RCS registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (projet d'acte constitutif)
Valid passport or national ID of each founder and of the intended Manager
Certificate of non-conviction (extrait du casier judiciaire) for each individual manager
Certified corporate documents and beneficial-ownership declaration if a corporate shareholder is present
Source-of-funds and wealth declaration (AML/KYC forms)
Bank account opening mandate and signature cards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises a KYC query, cure by promptly supplying updated beneficial-ownership declarations, corroborative source-of-funds evidence, and a written explanation of the corporate structure; the blocked-funds attestation is then re-issued within two business days of clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte Constitutif)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) acting under the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies; chamber of reference: Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the blocked-funds certificate and the final draft articles to the notary at least three working days before the signing. The notary verifies identity, legal capacity, criminal records, and the reality of the capital deposit, then reads and executes the deed. All founders and the appointed Manager (Gérant) sign the notarial minute; the notary issues certified excerpts (expéditions), the registered-office documentation, and the release instruction to the depositary bank. The criminal record extracts must be dated no more than three months prior to signature.
required_dossiers: Final notarial draft (minute) prepared by the notary
Original blocked-funds certificate from the depositary bank
Valid identity documents of all founders and the Manager
Criminal record extracts of the Manager and of any corporate directors
Written consent of the Manager accepting office, with specimen signature
Registered-office supporting documents (lease contract or domiciliation agreement, as applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in capacity, subscription, or capital conveyance, execute a corrective addendum (acte rectificatif) and re-authenticate the deed; any delay is managed by keeping the RCS filing deadline within the statutory period and immediately notifying the depositary bank of the revised signing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), e-filing desk at rcs.lbr.lu with physical submission of the notarial excerpt.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary e-files the certified excerpt of the deed together with the statutory annexes (pièces) on the LBR extranet, while the Company submits the Manager's signature card and the registered-office proof. Pay the LBR registration fee online. Legal personality of LU SARL is acquired upon RCS registration; the Company must obtain the RCS extract (Titre 1) showing the registration number BXXXXXX, which serves as proof of existence for bank, tax, and contracting counterparties. The depositary bank releases the blocked funds upon presentation of this certificate.
required_dossiers: Certified notarial excerpt (expédition) of the deed of incorporation
Nomination evidence and written acceptance of the Manager (Gérant)
Specimen signature card signed by the Manager
Proof of registered office (lease or professional domiciliation certificate)
Blocked-funds release certificate issued by the bank
LBR fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (demande de régularisation), file a mémoire en réponse with the requested corrective documents within the procedural deadline (generally 15 days) and refile the corrected annex; if registration is refused, appeal to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within one month of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal Publication in the RESA Electronic Company Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of incorporation, the notary submits the full notarial deed text for electronic publication in RESA. The Company must verify the online publication against the executed deed and archive the RESA pdf as the authoritative third-party notice. The publication completes the statutory publicity formalities and triggers the 3-month definitive-establishment period of the corporate veil.
required_dossiers: Full text of the notarised deed of incorporation
RCS registration number of LU SARL
Proof of RESA publication fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published text contains material errors, instruct the notary to file a corrective rectification declaration with LBR within the legal window; if the error is attributable to LBR's platform, obtain a correction free of charge and re-publish.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and National Identification Registration (ACD / AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Grand-Duché de Luxembourg; interfaces via MyGuichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, incorporation data is transmitted automatically to AEDT and ACD. The Company verifies receipt of its national identification number (numéro de matricule) and its Luxembourg VAT number (numéro de TVA). For ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511 software services, VAT registration is aligned with the expected B2B client base and payment rails (Swift Wire, Stripe); the Company submits the economic-activity declaration confirming the scope as kernel-level anti-cheat and integrity middleware, with principal place of supply in Luxembourg unless reverse charge applies. The Company also files the initial corporate tax registration parameters (fiscal year end, consolidating entity, manager identification).
required_dossiers: RCS extract (Titre 1) of LU SARL
Certified copy of the Articles of Association
Identity documents of the Manager and beneficial owners
Registered-office lease or domiciliation certificate
Detailed business-activity description mapping to ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511
Bank account details (IBAN and Swift confirmation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If no VAT number is received within the SLA, resubmit the VAT application via MyGuichet attaching the RCS extract and a business-activity memo; escalate to the AEDT taxpayer-service desk in Luxembourg-City for manual allocation of the due dates and retroactive effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Security Registration and Confirmation of License-Free Industry Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for occupational safety; Direction générale des PME, Ministère de l'Économie for the regulated-professions check.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register LU SARL as an employer with the CCSS within eight days before employing any staff and declare the Manager (Gérant) under the applicable occupational insurance scheme. Through the MyGuichet single-window, formally confirm that the anti-cheat software-development activity is not listed in the annex to the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to regulated professions and therefore requires no autorisation d'établissement. Maintain the workplace compliance file for the physical office, including ITM ergonomic and safety assessments for developer workstations.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
CCSS employer registration form (déclaration d'employeur)
Identity documents and personnel declaration for all employees and the Manager
Lease contract and physical-premises occupancy attestation
ITM workplace safety checklist and risk assessment
Confirmation note of non-regulated activity under the Law of 2 September 2011
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS rejects the employer file for data inconsistency, rectify the personnel declaration within five working days; if the Ministry of Economy nevertheless classifies an auxiliary service as regulated, file an application for autorisation d'établissement with good-standing documents, criminal-record extracts, and tax-clearance certificates, and appeal any refusal before the administrative courts within three months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction générale des PME, Ministère de l'Économie (Luxembourg), competent for establishment authorizations under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to regulated professions; activity confirmation is obtained via the MyGuichet unique window in consultation with the Chamber of Commerce.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — the ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511 kernel-level anti-cheat and integrity middleware development activity is not contained in the list of regulated professions annexed to the Law of 2 September 2011; no autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) is required, and the physical operation is covered by the general RCS registration and commercial-lease compliance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Protection Agency of Luxembourg), with technical support from the Administration de la gestion de l'eau (Water Management Administration).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / No statutory EIA — office-based software development is not an établissement classé under the Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments, and the activity falls outside the environmental-impact-assessment screening of the Law of 9 May 2014 on environmental assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous-waste streams are generated. The office operation is subject to municipal waste-separation obligations under the Law of 21 March 2017, WEEE take-back rules for electronic hardware, and prudent water-consumption practices. If an on-site server room is installed, cooling-water discharge, if any, must respect the general discharge parameters issued by the Water Management Administration, and backup-battery or fire-extinguishant handling must avoid release of hazardous substances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) through the commune's building-occupancy procedure for the registered office, including alarm systems, extinguishers, and evacuation plans; structural load inspection of the floor areas supporting server racks; occupational-safety statement filed with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering ergonomic workstations, ventilation, lighting, and emergency procedures; issuance of the municipal building-occupancy certificate (certificat de conformité) confirming the premises meet fire, safety, and physical-workplace requirements for the software-development operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT, registration duties and stamp taxes; Administration des douanes et accises for customs and excise matters. Principal digital portals: MyGuichet.lu (https://www.guichet.lu) for administrative filings, the Luxembourg Business Registers platform (https://www.lbr.lu) for RCS and business number issuance, and the ACD/AED e-filing services at impotsdirects.public.lu and aed.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SARL, the 13-digit national business identification number (matricule / numéro d'immatriculation) issued upon commercial registration is the statutory tax identifier and is obtained as follows: (1) execute the articles of association (statuts) before a Luxembourg notary, with a minimum share capital of EUR 12,500 of which at least 25% (EUR 3,125) must be paid in; foreign corporate shareholders are permitted without nationality restrictions; (2) file the incorporation dossier electronically with the RCS through the notary within one month of signature; (3) obtain the RCS registration and the matricule, which is automatically communicated to the ACD and AED; (4) use the matricule for all corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax declarations filed with the ACD via MyGuichet.lu; (5) submit the VAT registration application to the AED obtaining a Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU followed by 8 digits; (6) if employing staff, register as an employer with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS). A non-EU taxable person not established in Luxembourg must appoint a fiscal representative approved by the AED, whereas EU taxable persons may register directly without a local representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SARL is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune). Luxembourg City aggregate statutory charge approximates 22.8% (15% CIT plus 7% solidarity surcharge plus 6.75% municipal business tax before deductibility adjustments). Resident companies are taxed on worldwide income with relief through the participation exemption, double tax treaties and unilateral measures; the passive SPF holding regime is unavailable to an active ISIC 6201 software operating entity, and no territorial pass-through regime applies to SARLs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg; the SARL is per se an entity-level taxpayer and hybrid mismatch outcomes are determined non-electively under ATAD transposition. Available elective mechanisms include: (i) VAT fiscal unity (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law; (ii) optional joint taxation of municipal business tax for Luxembourg group companies with at least 95% direct or indirect ownership; (iii) the IP box election granting an 80% exemption on net qualifying IP income for grandfathered qualifying rights; (iv) the small business VAT exemption election under Article 130 limited to an annual turnover ceiling of EUR 35,000; (v) OSS and IOSS registrations for distance supplies of electronically supplied services and low-value imported goods; (vi) binding tax ruling and advance pricing agreement requests filed with the ACD covering transfer pricing, permanent establishment exposure and hybrid mismatch characterization; and (vii) DAC6 mandatory disclosure of reportable cross-border arrangements without any elective opt-out.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) is the national central bank and a Eurosystem member. Prudential supervision of banks, payment institutions and e-money institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), with significant Luxembourg credit institutions under the ECB Single Supervisory Mechanism. No exchange-control committee or foreign-investment approval authority exists in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility with zero exchange controls. Luxembourg applies no FX restrictions on either current-account items (royalties, licence fees, outsourcing) or capital-account items (share subscriptions, shareholder loans, dividends) under Article 63 TFEU. Profits may be remitted freely in EUR, USD or any permitted currency without BCL/CSSF authorisation; the only fiscal gate is Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (15% standard; 0% for qualifying corporate shareholders under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and the domestic participation-exemption regime; treaty-reduced rates otherwise). Bank-level sanctions and embargo screening are the sole operative constraints.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. As a euro-area state, Luxembourg imposes no export-proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion ratio and no repatriation deadline. The SARL may lawfully retain software-licensing receipts in USD, EUR or any convertible currency in Luxembourg or offshore. Banking practice requires only an economic-purpose narrative for BCL balance-of-payments statistics; no regulator mandates conversion or a holding period.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account with a blocked Capital Escrow Account (compte consignation) during incorporation and subsequent capital increases
Operational Account (EUR/USD/GBP) with SWIFT corporate e-banking and FX hedging documentation desk
Operational Account with SEPA/SWIFT clearing gateway and lender-grade treasury portal
Operational Account and ancillary Capital Escrow Account for shareholder injections

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High as a settlement channel, Low-Medium as a sole treasury hub. Luxembourg recognizes CSSF-licensed Payment Institutions and E-Money Institutions, and EEA-passported EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Revolut Business) may serve the SARL without a domestic licence; however, such institutions cannot lend, issue credit or hold funds beyond PSD2 limits on commercial accounts. Recommended deployment: Stripe (acting through an Irish-authorised Payment Institution under EEA passporting) as the card-acquiring collection rail; a global EMI IBAN as a low-cost FX sweep sub-account; and a domestic Tier-1 bank account as the anchor account that holds statutory capital, receives dividends and executes core liquidity clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No Luxembourg statute imposes a physical appearance for corporate account opening, but CSSF AML circulars require credit institutions to verify identity with adequate assurance. In practice, Tier-1 banks (BCEE, BGL BNP Paribas, BIL, ING) accept video-KYC and e-signature for EU-resident directors, while non-EU directors typically trigger an in-branch interview, a notarised power of attorney in favour of an EU-resident manager, or a certified-identity procedure via a Luxembourg notary. Plan for at least one director to attend a 45-minute onboarding meeting in Luxembourg at account opening; carry the RCSL extract, articles of association, UBO register extract, business plan and proof of business address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Gaming-adjacent merchant description: the anti-cheat middleware name references video-game integrity, which triggers elevated review by banks and Stripe as potential gambling exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCSL trade register extract and NACE/ISIC classification certificate confirming ISIC 6201 (computer programming); articles of association limiting the object to software licensing and middleware; two redacted customer contracts with non-gambling game publishers; product marketing deck clarifying anti-cheat integrity functions; an acceptable-use clause prohibiting deployment in online casinos; and a director's signed declaration on letterhead confirming the company does not serve gambling operators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU directors or 25%+ beneficial owners resident outside the EEA, requiring enhanced due diligence under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004, as amended.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled passport and proof of address for each non-EU director; 24-month personal bank statements; tax residence certificate; professional background CV; updated extract from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); and a source-of-wealth letter completed on the bank's prescribed form.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore intermediate holding (e.g., Hong Kong or UK company) sourcing the inbound capital, raising questions on corporate chain legitimacy and solvency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Holding-company audited financial statements; certificate of good standing; group organogram showing direct and indirect shareholdings; notarised board resolution approving the capital injection; subscription or loan agreement with economic terms; and confirmation of FATCA/CRS reporting classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Material royalty or licensing outflows above 25% of revenues in the first three years, creating a shadow-distribution and thin-capitalisation red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP licence agreements; OECD transfer-pricing file (master file and Luxembourg local file) demonstrating arm's-length royalty rates; royalty calculation workpapers; annual audited financial statements under Luxembourg GAAP; and a cash-flow forecast covering the service period.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Share capital is subscribed by wire to a blocked capital escrow account held with a Luxembourg credit institution before the notarial deed is signed; the mandatory EUR 12,000 SARL minimum capital must be fully paid in upon incorporation. For subsequent capital increases, the shareholder routes funds by SEPA Credit Transfer (EUR) or SWIFT MT103 with UETR (non-EUR) to the operational account, with field 70 populated as 'SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – SARL RESOLUTION [DATE]'. The receiving bank requires the notarised shareholders' resolution, updated articles, an updated share register, and the source-of-funds file. No BCL payment-purpose approval exists; the bank maps the narrative into its balance-of-payments statistical code for BCL reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EU/EEA supplier, payroll and subcontractor payments are executed via SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant (EUR); non-EUR and high-value payments use SWIFT MT103 with UETR, with invoice and contract references in field 70 (e.g., 'SOFTWARE LICENSE FEE PER AGREEMENT [INV] 2025-001'). Commercial letters of credit are structurally unsuitable for ISIC 6201 IP disbursements because the transaction lacks goods or bills of lading; where a customer demands documentary security, the bank issues an on-demand guarantee or standby LC. A daily or weekly FX forward programme sweeps surplus USD Stripe settlements into EUR for payroll and direct tax payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forwards (tenors up to 5 years) documented under an ISDA / 1998 FX Master Agreement with a CSSF-licensed banking counterparty
Deliverable EUR/USD FX swaps for short-term liquidity management and payroll-cycle mismatch
Cross-currency swaps between EUR and USD on a collateralised basis for IP-financing or intercompany-loan hedging

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally available in Luxembourg but generally inapplicable to EUR/USD because the euro is fully convertible; banks may quote NDFs solely for exotic non-convertible-currency receipts received from emerging-market licensees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (financial statements) filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of each financial year-end; final calendar-year SARL deadline is 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil and administrative penalties up to €5,000; risk of forced publication and management liability; prolonged non-filing triggers administrative strike-off of the SARL

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for intentional non-compliance; coercive administrative fines may also be imposed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined annual income tax return (CIT, municipal business tax and net wealth tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Normally due by 30 September of the following financial year for e-filed returns; extension available upon application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; late-filing penalty up to €1,000; possibility of best-of-judgment assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting (AGM) approval of annual accounts and discharge of managers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held within 6 months of each financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Managers may lose discharge protection; shareholders and creditors may bring liability claims; no direct monetary fine but corporate good-standing is affected

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL is exempt from statutory audit unless it exceeds two of the three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total > €4.4 million; net turnover > €8.8 million; average headcount > 50. Always-audited categories include banks, insurance undertakings, and regulated funds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Luxembourg legal accounting framework) for statutory annual accounts; EU-IFRS mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups and optional for statutory individual accounts; small SARLs may file abbreviated formats.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every SARL must file an annual RBE confirmation before 15 March of each calendar year. If a share transfer changes beneficial ownership, a separate updated declaration must be filed within one month of the transfer being registered. The annual confirmation verifies continued accuracy and does not replace event-based UBO updates.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate rate in Luxembourg City, composed of 17% corporate income tax (for taxable income above EUR 200,000), 1.19% employment-fund solidarity surcharge (7% levied on the 17% CIT), and 6.75% municipal business tax; lower CIT brackets apply below EUR 200,000 (15% up to EUR 175,000 and 16% between EUR 175,001 and EUR 200,000).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains on shareholdings of at least 10% held for 12 months; IP box under Article 50ter LIR: 80% deduction for qualifying nexus-restricted IP income; R&D tax credit up to 25% of eligible research expenditure; investment tax credit of 8% on the first investment tranche and 13% on the excess; the aggregate headline rate exceeds the 15% OECD Pillar Two minimum, so a gaming anti-cheat group within Pillar Two scope would not incur a Luxembourg top-up tax on ordinary profits.
